 ‘Maybe one more’ – Crawford teases a comeback and calls out Garcia at 160lbs
 Written by BBN Editor on 4th November 2026.
 Key points: 
 Terence Crawford, retired and unbeaten since December 2025, wrote on X on November 4: “Maybe one more!” and then “What’s up Ryan Garcia, 160?” 
 He followed up with a jibe at Garcia’s interest in a Floyd Mayweather fight: “My bad, you got Mayweather to focus on I forgot” 
 Crawford, 39, has not announced a signed comeback, and Garcia holds the WBC welterweight title at 147lbs 
 Garcia pressed Mayweather publicly on October 30, and has also been linked with Teofimo Lopez in early 2027 
 Terence Crawford, a year into his retirement, has teased a return, and named the man he wants.
 “Maybe one more!” Crawford posted on X . He then tagged Ryan Garcia: “What’s up Ryan Garcia, 160?” and added: “My bad, you got Mayweather to focus on I forgot.”
 What Crawford said 
 The 39-year-old retired in December 2025 as an undisputed champion in three weight classes, with five world titles across divisions, joining Mayweather, Andre Ward, and Joe Calzaghe as a fighter who retired unbeaten. In September, he told Garcia he liked him because he’s funny, and asked why he never called him out when he was active. This is his first message that suggests he’s considering a return.
 The weight 
 Garcia won the WBC welterweight title in February by beating Mario Barrios. Crawford’s proposal of 160lbs, the middleweight limit, is 13lbs above the welterweight limit, with 154lbs in between. The middleweight championships aren’t at stake, and Crawford hasn’t announced a signed fight.
 Garcia’s options 
 Garcia pressed Mayweather publicly on October 30, saying he wants a professional fight and rejecting an exhibition. Mayweather hasn’t confirmed. Garcia has also been linked with a unification with Teofimo Lopez in early 2027. Crawford’s last fight was his September 2025 win over Canelo Alvarez, who has just regained the WBC super middleweight title.
